market_view: South African shares jumped 4.8% in a four-session week, led by gold miners and Naspers after the US midterms and SA's local elections, while the rand firmed to R16.48/$ and the 10-year yield eased to near 8.60%, with the repo rate at 7.25% ahead of the November MPC. In New York the S&P 500 fell 2.7% and the Nasdaq 3.4% in their worst week since June as fears that a Democratic Congress will curb AI and data-centre spending hit chip and storage stocks, with October CPI on 10 Nov the next test after September's 3.7%. Gold rose 4.5% and platinum 6.9% while Brent fell about 16% to $98 a barrel, so investors should expect choppier markets in which SA resources and rand-hedge shares can cushion the swings while richly valued tech stays vulnerable.
